windows.reason: WITHDRAWN by the 2026-08-20 root-cause investigation -- DO NOT APPROVE. The earlier case for this waiver ('the obstacle is the Windows ROCm toolchain, a gfx-specific rocBLAS/Tensile fallback kernel for the value head's small GEMM shapes') has been FALSIFIED. The defect is a latent host-side stream-ordering bug in lc0's own weight-upload path, not a toolchain defect, and it is fixable in the port. allocAndUpload (src/neural/backends/cuda/layers.cc) launches copyTypeConverted on the legacy null stream, reading the shared scratch buffer, and returns without waiting; every compute stream is created cudaStreamNonBlocking so nothing orders that copy against the first evaluation, which overwrites the same scratch. The last upload of the last-constructed layer -- the value head's ip2_val_b_ -- loses the race, so exactly one 3-float bias is corrupted while every computed tensor around it is exact. Windows HIP loses this race deterministically where Linux HIP wins it. Measured on windows-gfx1151 at head 7727fa3: the dense-2 GEMM output equals a host double-precision reference exactly, the device bias reads -1.40802431 0.55243015 0.00000000 against the net's 0.43719077 -0.98977518 0.55311656, and adding cudaStreamSynchronize(0) at the end of allocAndUpload takes the gate check from 0/222 to 222/222 passing (value abs 6.0e-08, was 4.4e-02). rocBLAS/hipBLASLt was independently exonerated (ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0 changes nothing). Full evidence in projects/lc0/notes.md, section 'Investigation 2026-08-20 (windows-gfx1151) -- why Windows'. The correct route is a moat-fix-<pr#> round carrying the one-line fix, not a gate waiver; this suggestion is retained only to overwrite the falsified reasoning that stood here.
windows.refused_note: Refused on the 2026-08-20 root-cause evidence, which falsified the waiver's own rationale. The obstacle is NOT the Windows ROCm toolchain and NOT a gfx-specific rocBLAS/Tensile kernel: it is a latent host-side stream-ordering race in lc0's own code. allocAndUpload (src/neural/backends/cuda/layers.cc) memcpys into the shared scratch buffer, launches copyTypeConverted on the legacy null stream, and returns without synchronising; every compute stream is created cudaStreamNonBlocking, so nothing orders that copy against the first evaluation, which overwrites the same scratch. Only the last upload of the last-constructed layer survives to be observed, which for a classic net with no moves-left head is the value head's 3-float bias ip2_val_b_. Windows only loses the race because its KMD defers submission; the Linux KFD path lands the copy immediately. Verified fix is one line -- cudaStreamSynchronize(0) after the copy -- taking the gate from 0/222 to 222/222 and the value error from 4.4e-02 to 6.0e-08. Do not waive a real, fixable bug in our own port. Land the fix as a moat-fix-2420 round against open PR #2420, revalidate, and take the windows gate honestly.
